title: Licence or key in an official-or-better price series
problem: Nothing on this site can compute ROI, closing-line value or staking performance, because no price exists. Every payoff column is empty.
paths: A: buy a commercial odds archive. B: key the opening and closing numbers in weekly from one sportsbook at a fixed hour. C: do nothing and keep the leaderboard price-free.
tradeoffs: A is accurate and auditable but costs money. B is free and reproducible but depends on one person's discipline. C costs nothing and caps what the project can ever prove.
unlocks: Unlocks ROI, CLV, drawdown, Kelly staking, the demotion gates D3 and partly D1, and a real leaderboard.

title: Add an official per-game player-statistics capture to CI
problem: The four player-prop-combo strategies (R1-R4) cannot be scored at all: the repository holds no per-game player numbers.
paths: A: capture nfl.com player game logs. B: capture nfl.com weekly team/player stat leaders only. C: drop prop strategies from scope.
tradeoffs: A is the only route to genuine prop markets. B is cheap but covers a handful of players. C removes a whole strategy family the brief asks for.
unlocks: Unlocks the prop-combo family and the injury-to-target-share link.

title: Capture the as-of date on each club depth chart
problem: 0 of the captured charts carry an as-of date and most are labelled unofficial by the club, so the depth layer cannot be audited.
paths: A: scrape the chart page's own updated-on text. B: use the NFL's official weekly transaction report as the clock instead. C: leave undated and keep the layer advisory.
tradeoffs: A depends on each club's page markup. B is uniform across clubs and comes from the league. C is honest but weak evidence.
unlocks: Makes the 2nd/3rd/4th-string layer auditable rather than indicative.

title: Backfill injury reports for weeks 1-7
problem: The availability layer covers 3 of 10 played weeks, which is why no availability coefficient is fitted.
paths: A: backfill from the same official injury pages. B: start fresh next season. C: keep the 3-week window.
tradeoffs: A triples the sample immediately. B delays the payoff a year. C leaves the requirement only partly served.
unlocks: Triples the availability sample and is the precondition for S-08.

title: Decide the sample-size gate: keep 200 or lower it
problem: At 137 finals nothing can clear a 200-decision gate, so the leaderboard is empty by construction.
paths: A: keep 200 and wait. B: lower to 100 with a wider interval. C: publish a provisional tier below the gate, labelled as such.
tradeoffs: A is the most rigorous and the slowest. B raises the false-positive rate. C gives the leaderboard something to show without claiming skill.
unlocks: Determines when the leaderboard can ever be non-empty.

title: Publish an interval on the home-field constant
problem: The constant is refitted weekly and printed as a bare number, so a reader cannot tell movement from noise.
paths: A: bootstrap interval. B: report the week-by-week series and let the reader see the spread. C: fix it at a conventional value.
tradeoffs: A is the most informative. B is cheap and honest. C throws away a measured quantity.
unlocks: Makes the home-field strategy S8 scoreable.

title: Replace the normal margin model with the empirical distribution
problem: NFL margins cluster on 3 and 7, so a normal CDF misprices the moneyline near those numbers.
paths: A: empirical CDF from verified finals. B: a discrete key-number model. C: keep the normal approximation and flag it.
tradeoffs: A is exact but needs a large sample. B is the industry-standard fix. C is the cheapest and least accurate.
unlocks: Improves moneyline calibration, which feeds the Brier skill score.

title: Fit the availability coefficient walk-forward once the injury weeks are backfilled
problem: The injury-and-depth layer is published but never enters a line, because its coefficient is not identified on 3 weeks.
paths: A: fit walk-forward with a ridge penalty. B: fit per unit (offense, defense). C: leave the layer advisory forever.
tradeoffs: A is the standard approach. B is more expressive but needs more data. C keeps the layer honest but inert.
unlocks: Turns the depth tracker into a model input instead of a report.

title: Decide the leaderboard reward structure
problem: Rewards are notional. Paying on an unvalidated signal funds luck.
paths: A: notional only until a strategy clears every blocking gate. B: small fixed monthly prize pool. C: tiered, paid only on signal score.
tradeoffs: A is the safe default. B pays for participation. C rewards the thing we actually want but needs a validated signal first.
unlocks: Makes the competition real without paying for noise.

title: Handle neutral-site games explicitly
problem: The model applies the same home-field constant to neutral-site games, where there is no home field.
paths: A: fit a separate neutral-site constant. B: zero the home field for those games. C: exclude them from grading.
tradeoffs: A needs a big neutral-site sample. B is a defensible prior. C loses real games from the record.
unlocks: Removes a known bias on the international and neutral-site slate.

title: Wire every module's verifier into one CI job
problem: Different modules have different verifiers and pages.yml does not run all of them, so a regression can pass CI.
paths: A: one job that runs every verifier. B: one workflow per module. C: leave as is.
tradeoffs: A is the only way to guarantee a single definition of green. B is modular but the union is never checked. C is the status quo.
unlocks: Makes 'the site builds with no broken links' a checked statement rather than an asserted one.

title: Retire the thirteen overlapping site trees behind one navigation
problem: Thirteen separate trees built by earlier sessions all present similar tables with different numbers, and only one is maintained.
paths: A: keep one canonical tree and move the rest to an archive index. B: merge the tables into one canonical register. C: leave all thirteen live.
tradeoffs: A is a small change with a large clarity gain. B is the right end state but a large job. C guarantees the next reader finds conflicting numbers.
unlocks: Stops the same question having thirteen different answers on the same site.
